tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.thinking:
I'm laying out the plan for the attachment types in lib/ai/chat-attachments.ts, starting with images and PDFs and then the Office formats.

I'm settling on the XLS question: the exceljs library can't read the old BIFF format, and parsing OLE2 compound files by hand isn't cheap, so I'll skip XLS and record that as a decision. For CSV and TSV there's no magic number to sniff, so I'm going to check that the bytes are text, decoding UTF-8 first and falling back to Windows-1252 since German bank exports often use it.

I'm weighing whether jszip, which exceljs already pulls in, or fflate is the right zip reader, and checking node_modules for either. For the Office XML I'm leaning toward a small hand-written tag tokenizer over regex, picking out paragraphs, heading styles, text runs, tabs, and line breaks.

I'm checking which zip reader is already installed, since jszip comes in through exceljs and fflate would be sync. The zip sniff will look for the main content types in [Content_Types].xml to tell DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX apart, and I'm skipping the macro-enabled variants.

I'm checking whether `@napi-rs/canvas`, which `unpdf`'s page rendering needs in Node, is already installed. If it isn't, adding a native dependency raises packaging questions for the Electron desktop build. The alternative is pulling the embedded scan images straight out of each PDF page and PNG-encoding them myself with Node's built-in zlib.

I'm checking whether `@napi-rs/canvas` is already in node_modules and how the desktop build packages native modules, since that decides whether rendering scanned PDF pages is a reasonable dependency to add.

### Use your Claude plan (optional)

Moneo can run on your Claude subscription instead of an API key. It uses Claude Code, which comes with Moneo, signed in with your own Claude account on this computer. Moneo never sees or stores your Claude login; Claude Code keeps it, the same one the Claude Code app uses.

1. In **Settings → AI access**, click **Sign in with Claude** on this computer. A Claude sign-in page opens in your browser.
2. Sign in. If the page shows a code, paste it into Moneo and click **Continue**. If you're already signed in to Claude Code, Moneo shows your account straight away; click **Use Claude plan**.

Chat, artifacts, briefings, imports and the agents then run on Claude (Opus 5.5 for the chat, Haiku 5.5 for lighter tasks; change them under **Settings → AI and your data → Advanced**). Requests count toward your plan's usage limits, shown at [claude.ai/settings/usage](https://claude.ai/settings/usage).

- **Never billed to an API key.** Moneo removes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and similar settings before it starts Claude Code, and only runs Claude when Claude Code is signed in with a Claude plan. If you sign out of Claude Code, AI stays off until you sign in again or pick another option.
- **Only Moneo's tools.** Claude gets Moneo's finance tools and nothing else: no files, no shell, no other MCP servers, and no chat history saved by Claude Code. Changes still go through cards you accept.
- **PDFs in chat** are read on your computer and sent to Claude as text. A scanned PDF has no text to read, so attach photos of its pages instead.
- **Not yet:** voice calls and dictation, which still need an OpenAI API key for the audio.
- **Stop using Claude** switches Moneo back to ChatGPT or your API key. It doesn't sign you out of Claude Code.
- Anthropic's rules say apps may not offer Claude plan sign-in without its approval ([Agent SDK overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview)). Moneo only uses the Claude Code login you set up yourself, on your own computer. Decide for yourself whether that fits your use.

content.content:
## Everyday use

- **Start Moneo:** `npm start` in the Moneo folder (Docker Desktop must be running).
- **Stop Moneo:** press `Ctrl+C`. The database keeps running in Docker; `docker compose stop` stops it.
- **Update Moneo:**
  ```sh
  git pull
  npm ci
  npm run setup
  npm run build
  npm start
  ```
  Your data and secrets are kept.

While Moneo runs it does its background work by itself: scheduled summaries, and syncing your bank and Scalable about once a day. Anything missed while your computer was off runs shortly after you start Moneo.

Opening Moneo or coming back to it also syncs in the background (Scalable at most every 15 minutes, banks at most every hour): you see the last numbers right away and the page updates when the sync lands. If a value can't be refreshed, it still counts in your net worth and Wealth marks it as not from today. A short message in the corner of Home tells you once about old values and about a connection that failed or needs reconnecting.

## Good to know

- Moneo only listens on `127.0.0.1`, so other devices on your network can't open it unless you turn on [phone and tablet access](#use-it-from-your-phone-or-tablet-optional).
- Your data lives in the Docker volumes `moneo_db-data` and `moneo_storage-data`. `docker compose down` keeps them; **`docker compose down -v` deletes all your data**.
- If ports 54321 or 54322 are already in use, add `API_PORT=` and `DB_PORT=` with free ports to `.env` and run `npm run setup` again.

content.thinking:
I'm planning to split this into three commits, since some files depend on others and the split has to stay clean. The first covers reading documents on the computer, including the types, extraction, storage, message, chat route, and test changes. The second would be the document_read tool and its labels, but those live in the same route file, so I'll fold them into the first commit. The third is for citations.

I'm grouping the rest of the work into the citations commit: the citations module, the chips, the viewer, the section route, the ai-message and chat-messages components, the prompt, and the voice strip. Docs (README and the app guide) get their own commit after that. Citations being in the read code is fine, so the first commit can keep it as it is.

input.command:
git add lib/ai/documents/read.ts app/api/chat/route.ts lib/ai/claude.ts lib/ai/claude.test.ts components/ai-tool-activity.tsx && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Read Word, PowerPoint, Excel and CSV attachments on every AI source

Chat attachments now take DOCX, PPTX, XLSX and CSV/TSV besides photos and
PDFs, up to 25 MB each (the 4 MB serverless limit no longer applies). The
real type is still sniffed from the bytes; Office files are checked by the
main part in [Content_Types].xml.

Every document becomes text on the owner's computer the same way for every
source, with locations: PDF pages, PPTX slides with speaker notes, numbered
DOCX paragraphs with headings, and sheets as compact tables with row numbers
and column letters. PDF pages without a text layer are drawn as JPEG images
(at most 10 per message) instead of asking for photos. Long documents are cut
with a note naming the next range.

The new read-only document_read tool reopens any file attached earlier in
the conversation by id, by location range or by text search; earlier files
are listed with their ids. Extracted text is cached in memory by path.

The Claude-only PDF path is gone now that the shared path covers it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git add -A lib/ai/citations.test.ts app/api/chat/attachments/section components/citation-chip.tsx components/ai-message.tsx components/ai-message.test.tsx components/chat-messages.tsx lib/ai/provider.ts lib/ai/voice-call-controller.ts lib/ai/voice-call-controller.test.ts && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Cite attached files with chips that open the cited place

The model cites a file right after a sentence as {{cite ID LOCATION "quote"}}.
The chat turns valid markers that point to a file in this conversation into
small chips such as "statement.pdf · p.3" or "budget.xlsx · Sheet1!B12";
others are dropped. PDFs and photos open in the browser (a PDF at its page);
Word, PowerPoint and spreadsheet citations open a viewer showing the cited
paragraphs, slide or cells with the quote highlighted. Voice calls leave the
markers out of what they say.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git add README.md lib/ai/app-guide.ts && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Document chat attachments and citations

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
